walkthroughs.body_html: Sgr A* is the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, about 4 million solar masses. Its mass was measured by tracking stars (like S2) orbiting close to it — work that won Genzel and Ghez the 2020 Nobel Prize.
The black hole mass correlates tightly with the host bulge's velocity dispersion. This M-sigma relation suggests galaxies and their black holes co-evolve through feedback.
The Event Horizon Telescope imaged the shadow of M87* in 2019 and Sgr A* in 2022 — both confirming Einstein's predictions about black hole appearance.
